blocks.text: Use the page IDs to find things. They stay the same when pages are added. Numbered instructions are steps; the action cost is shown separately. Use my character sheet for current bonuses, DCs, defenses, HP, Speeds and equipment.

pages.title: My turn

blocks.title: Start my turn
steps: End my previous directive’s bonuses (C9). Reset my actions, reaction and NEXT ATTACK marker on C8.
Check conditions. Slowed or stunned can reduce my available actions.
Choose what I want to accomplish. Ask about an unfamiliar action before committing.

blocks.title: End my turn
steps: Resolve persistent damage and recovery checks. Usually reduce frightened by 1. Keep my reaction available for its trigger.

pages.lead: I have 3 actions each turn. A Strike is one weapon or unarmed attack. Spend actions in any order. Use the current numbers on my character sheet.
pages.source: Core pp. 104, 428–429 • Current numbers: character sheet

blocks.title: Delay
blocks.cost: Free action • only when my turn begins
blocks.before: I have not taken actions on this turn.
steps: Say that I am delaying. My turn pauses; I leave the initiative order.
After another creature finishes its turn, choose to return. Take my turn then. My new initiative position stays there.
blocks.note: While waiting: I cannot use reactions. Negative start- and end-of-turn effects happen now. Benefits due to end during my turn end now too. After a whole round, I lose the held turn and keep my original initiative.

blocks.title: Ready
blocks.before: One available single action or untriggered free action.
steps: Name a clear, observable trigger and the action I will take. Readying ends my turn.
If the trigger occurs before my next turn, spend my reaction to take that action. Its requirements must still be met.
blocks.note: A readied attack uses the attack penalty I had when I readied it. I can Ready a pistol or neural-lash Strike. Concentrate: Ready requires focus.

blocks.text: Choose Delay to take my whole turn after an ally sets something up. Choose Ready to reserve one specific action for a trigger.

pages.title: Four usable turns

blocks.text: Each row spends three actions. Choose the row that fits the situation.
Size Up asset? Lead by Example costs 1 action total against that asset, including its attack (Y1). This leaves one more action available.
Check first: weapon ready and loaded; target in range; no directive already issued this round. An attack inside an activity still counts toward my attack penalty.

pages.source: Core pp. 104, 108, 408–410 • Bon Mot: PF Core 2 p. 228

pages.title: Choose my next action
pages.lead: Use this when I want a starting point. I can choose a different approach.

blocks.text: Before committing: check range, free hands, actions left and whether I already used a directive this round. Ask the GM about anything uncertain.
Already attacked? Another attack takes a penalty. Bon Mot, Demoralize, a directive without a Strike, and Take Cover do not increase that penalty.

pages.source: Decision aid • action rules on the referenced pages

pages.title: Get ’Em!

blocks.text: Requirements for either version: one visible enemy within 60 feet; allies can hear my call or see my signal; my directive is available this round.

blocks.title: Focus our attacks
steps: Name the enemy and give the order.
Place the +1 ATTACK token on C9 and write the target’s name. I and my allies add +1 status to attack rolls against it.
blocks.note: Issuing the order requires no roll.

blocks.title: Lead by Example
blocks.cost: 2 actions total • includes one weapon attack
steps: Name the enemy and give the order. Place +1 ATTACK on C9: I and my allies get +1 status to attacks against it.
Make one Strike. Include the +1 in my attack roll. On a hit, add my Charisma modifier as status damage. Spend the weapon’s ammunition.
After that attack, place DAMAGE on C9. Hit or miss, our later Strikes against this enemy gain the status damage bonus below.
blocks.before: Weapon held and ready; enemy within its reach or range. A pistol must be loaded.

blocks.text: Both versions: move DIRECTIVE to ISSUED on C8. All bonuses end at the start of my next turn. Get ’Em! and Digital Assessment! share the one directive per round limit.
Size Up asset: Lead by Example costs 1 action total against that asset. Follow the same three steps (Y1).

pages.source: Core pp. 104, 108 • attack penalty and range still apply

blocks.text: Requirements: target within 100 feet; allies can hear my call or see my signal; my directive is available this round.

blocks.title: Find a useful fact
steps: Ask one question and suggest a skill that fits. Agree on the skill before spending the action.
The GM secretly rolls. Use the result below. If I identify the creature successfully, also learn one resistance or immunity.
results: Success: answer to my question. Critical success: extra information. Failure: none. Critical failure: possibly false information.
blocks.note: Concentrate: the included Recall Knowledge needs focus.

blocks.title: Assess and defend
blocks.cost: 2 actions total • assessment and one weapon attack
steps: Make the assessment above, then make one Strike. Apply my current attack penalty and spend the weapon’s ammunition. Advance NEXT ATTACK (C8).
Place +1 AC on C9 and write the target. I and my allies gain +1 circumstance AC against its attacks until my next turn starts. This applies even if my check or attack failed.
If the creature has the tech trait, it rolls Fortitude vs my Class DC on my sheet. Failure: glitching 1. It then becomes immune to Digital Assessment! for 1 hour.
blocks.before: Weapon held and ready; target within its reach or range. A pistol must be loaded.

blocks.text: After either version, move DIRECTIVE to ISSUED (C8). Choose a knowledge skill that fits the question; use its current modifier from my sheet.

pages.title: Weaken an enemy

blocks.title: Bon Mot
blocks.before: Foe within 30 feet can hear me, understand my language, and be affected by emotion and mental effects.
steps: Deliver a distracting quip. Roll Diplomacy vs its Will DC.
blocks.note: Record each affected person, penalty and end time on C9. Place BON MOT there while any effect remains. The target can end its penalty with a one-action concentrated retort or suitable skill action. The penalty also lowers Will and Perception DCs. Concentrate: needs focus.
results: Success: target takes –2 status to Perception and Will for 1 minute. Critical success: –3. Failure: no effect.
Critical failure: I take –2 to Perception and Will for 1 minute, or until I succeed at another Bon Mot.

blocks.title: Demoralize
blocks.before: A creature I am aware of is within 30 feet, can hear me, and can be affected by fear, emotion and mental effects.
steps: Shout or threaten. Roll Intimidation vs its Will DC. Take –4 circumstance if I use a language it does not understand, or a wordless shout.
blocks.note: After any result, the target is immune to my Demoralize for 10 minutes. Frightened reduces checks and DCs, including attacks, saves and AC; usually decreases by 1 at its turn’s end. Auditory, concentrate: sound and focus.
results: Success: frightened 1. Critical success: frightened 2. Failure: no effect.

blocks.text: Size Up: add +1 circumstance against an asset. These actions have no attack trait, so they do not increase my attack penalty.

pages.source: Bon Mot: PF Core 2 p. 228 • SF Core p. 200

blocks.title: Aid
blocks.cost: Usually 1 action to prepare; reaction to help
blocks.before: An ally accepts my help; the GM approves my method.
steps: Name the ally’s upcoming attack roll or skill check and explain how I help. Spend the preparation action.
When the ally is about to roll, spend my reaction. Roll the skill or attack the GM selected. Typical DC 15; the GM can adjust it.
outcomes: Ally gets +2 circumstance; +3 if I am master with the check, +4 if legendary.
blocks.note: The method determines traits and any resource cost. Helping with gunfire may spend a bullet; agree first. Aid normally boosts a roll, not a spell DC or an enemy’s saving throw.

blocks.title: No Cause for Alarm
blocks.before: Frightened creatures within 10 feet can hear and understand me. They must be affected by emotion and mental effects.
steps: Reassure them. Roll Diplomacy once; compare it with each affected creature’s Will DC.
blocks.note: This includes enemies who qualify. Concentrate: needs focus.
results: Success: reduce frightened by 1. Critical success: reduce it by 2. Failure: no change. Each target is immune to this ability for 1 hour.

blocks.title: Apply a commercial medpatch
blocks.cost: 1 action if held • 1 more action to draw it
blocks.before: Patch held in one usable hand; target within reach. It must be willing, paralyzed, petrified or unconscious.
steps: Apply the patch to me or the target. No Medicine roll.
Target regains 1d6 HP, up to maximum HP, and gets +1 item to disease and poison saves for 10 minutes. Cross off one patch.
blocks.note: Consumable: used up. Tech: if this patch is glitching, check V3 first. Manipulate: needs usable hands or gestures; can trigger reactions. If grabbed, pass a DC 5 flat check or lose the action.

blocks.title: Administer First Aid
blocks.before: Adjacent patient; medkit worn or held. A worn medkit needs one free hand; a held one needs two.
blocks.note: Manipulate: needs usable hands or gestures; can trigger reactions. If grabbed, pass a DC 5 flat check or lose the action.
choices: Stabilize a dying creature at 0 HP: roll Medicine vs 15 + dying value (normally). Success removes dying; patient stays unconscious at 0 HP. Critical failure increases dying by 1.

Stop persistent bleeding: roll Medicine vs the effect’s DC. Success gives assisted recovery with a lower recovery DC. Critical failure deals an immediate tick of bleed damage. Failure changes nothing.

blocks.text: Treat Wounds takes 10 minutes (G5). Battle Medicine requires its own feat. Restoring HP to a dying ally is often the quickest way to help (V4).

pages.title: Shoot and reload

blocks.title: Semi-auto pistol: Strike
blocks.before: Loaded pistol in one hand; target in range.
steps: Use my sheet’s attack modifier, then the penalties below.
Roll d20 + modifier vs AC. Hit: use my sheet’s damage. Critical hit: double it, including bonuses.
Move 1 bullet LOADED → SPENT (C3), hit or miss. Advance NEXT ATTACK (C8).
blocks.note: Analog: immune to tech-targeting effects. Shots can trigger reactions.

blocks.text: Three attack modifiers listed? Use the matching one; its penalty is included. Get ’Em!: +1 status against its target.

blocks.title: Reload the pistol
blocks.before: A free hand and ammunition available.
steps: Return tokens to empty LOADED spaces (C3); subtract that many bullets from my reserve.
blocks.note: Manipulate: can trigger reactions; grabbed requires flat DC 5 or I lose the action.

pages.source: Core pp. 253–255, 265 • See C3 for tracker

blocks.title: Neural lash: Strike
steps: Choose mental or slashing damage. For objects or mindless creatures, choose slashing.
Choose nonlethal (knock out a living foe at 0 HP) or lethal. Both use the same attack bonus.
Use the lash’s attack modifier on my sheet. Apply my attack penalty (B1) once. With Get ’Em!, add +1.
Hit: roll my sheet’s lash damage, using the chosen damage type. Critical hit: double damage and normal bonuses. Advance NEXT ATTACK (C8), hit or miss.
blocks.before: Lash held in one hand; target within 5 feet.

blocks.text: Thought — GM ruling: Ponder Unity counts as telepathy. I can ignore unwieldy: repeated lash attacks and a readied lash attack are allowed. I can also ignore nonlethal to deal lethal damage without a penalty.
Versatile S: slashing is an option each attack. Analog: immune to effects specifically targeting technology. All my attacks share the same attack count.
Make a hand available

blocks.title: Release
steps: Let go of an item or release one hand from a two-handed item. A dropped item stays on the ground.
blocks.note: Manipulate: grabbed requires flat DC 5. Release does not trigger manipulate reactions.

blocks.text: Interact — 1 action: draw, pick up or put away an item; swap a held item for another; or add a hand to my grip. Needs a usable hand; can trigger reactions; grabbed requires flat DC 5.

blocks.title: Stride or Step
blocks.note: Move: Stride can trigger movement reactions; Step avoids them. Diagonal squares cost 5 feet, then 10 feet, alternating through my turn.
choices: Stride: move up to my Speed on my sheet. Ordinary difficult terrain costs 10 feet per square; greater difficult terrain costs 15 feet.
Step: move 5 feet without triggering movement reactions. Needs Speed 10+; cannot enter difficult terrain or use my climb Speed.

blocks.title: Take Cover
blocks.before: I have cover, a suitable nearby feature, or I am prone.
steps: With standard cover, improve to greater cover: +4. Otherwise gain standard cover: +2.
Add this circumstance bonus to AC, Reflex saves against areas, and Stealth to avoid detection.
blocks.note: Ends if I move, attack, fall unconscious or end it for free. A creature between us usually gives lesser cover: +1 AC only. The GM decides whether I can improve it.

pages.title: Create a distraction

blocks.title: Create a Diversion
blocks.before: Choose creatures who can notice the distraction and are not immune to mental effects.
steps: Use words, a gesture or a trick. Roll Deception once vs each target’s Perception DC.
blocks.note: Failure: no distraction; the target knows I tried. All targets get +4 circumstance to their Perception DC against my diversions for 1 minute, whatever the result.
results: Success: I become hidden from that creature until my turn ends, unless I reveal myself first.
While hidden this way, I can Step, Hide or Sneak. A Strike gets the benefit of hidden for that one attack, then reveals me. Other actions normally reveal me before I act.

blocks.title: Digital Diversion
blocks.cost: 1 action • a different way to Create a Diversion
blocks.before: I am adjacent to the target. It carries, wears or wields a tech item. My hacking toolkit is worn or held, and I have a free hand.
steps: Cause a ping or warning on the target’s equipment.
Use Computers instead of Deception. Resolve the same diversion results and 1-minute repeat penalty above.
blocks.note: My toolkit must be accessible. Use the same mental and manipulate restrictions below.

blocks.text: Trait checks: words need hearing and a shared language. A gesture or trick has manipulate: usable hands; may trigger reactions; grabbed requires a DC 5 flat check. Mental effects do not affect mindless creatures.

pages.source: Core pp. 198, 218 • Digital Diversion requirements verified online

blocks.title: Hide
blocks.before: I have standard/greater cover, or concealment, from each creature I try to hide from.
steps: The GM compares my Stealth result with observers’ Perception DCs. Add cover’s circumstance bonus when it helps me hide.
blocks.note: Leaving cover/concealment reveals me. Hidden normally ends before an action other than Hide, Sneak or Step; one Strike benefits first, then reveals me.
results: Success: hidden from that observer. It knows my space but must pass a DC 11 flat check to target me. It is off-guard to me. Failure: still observed.

blocks.title: Sneak
blocks.before: I am hidden or undetected from the creatures I want to evade.
steps: Move up to half my Speed. Finish with cover or concealment unless the GM allows another method.
blocks.note: Move: can trigger movement reactions. Step is the exception. If plainly visible at the end, I am observed. Sneak can also work while unseen and already undetected.
results: Success: undetected. Failure: hidden, but they know my new space. Critical failure: observed.

blocks.text: Grabbed / restrained: off-guard and unable to move. Grabbed: manipulate needs flat DC 5. Restrained: no attack/manipulate actions except Escape or Force Open the bonds.

blocks.title: Escape
blocks.before: Grabbed, restrained or otherwise immobilized.
steps: Roll Acrobatics, Athletics or unarmed attack vs the Escape DC. Apply my attack penalty.
blocks.note: Advance NEXT ATTACK (C8). No manipulate flat check.
results: Success: free. Critical success: also Stride 5 feet. Failure: still caught. Critical failure: no more Escape attempts until my next turn.

blocks.title: Drop Prone / Stand / Crawl
blocks.note: These move actions can trigger movement reactions.
choices: Drop Prone: off-guard; –2 circumstance to attacks. Take Cover gives +4 AC vs ranged attacks; off-guard still applies.
Stand: end prone. Crawl: move 5 feet while prone; needs Speed 10+.

blocks.title: Leap
steps: Jump 10 feet across with Speed 15–25, or 15 feet with Speed 30+. Include the landing space. Or jump 3 feet up, 5 feet across. No roll.
blocks.note: Move: can trigger reactions. Longer jumps need Athletics.

blocks.title: Avert Gaze
steps: Until my next turn: +2 circumstance to saves against visual abilities that require looking at them.

blocks.title: Feint
blocks.before: An enemy is within my melee reach and can be affected by mental effects.
steps: Mislead the enemy. Roll Deception vs its Perception DC.
blocks.note: Feint leaves my attack count unchanged. Its benefit applies to melee attacks, including the lash.
results: Success: off-guard to my next melee attack this turn. Critical success: to all my melee attacks through my next turn.
Failure: no change. Critical failure: I am off-guard to its melee attacks through my next turn.

blocks.title: Tumble Through
steps: Stride up to my Speed. To move through one enemy’s space, roll Acrobatics against its Reflex DC.
blocks.note: Move: can trigger reactions.
results: Success: pass through. Its space is difficult terrain. I need enough movement to get all the way through.
Failure, or too little movement: stop before entering its space. I trigger reactions as though I moved out of my starting square.

blocks.title: Point Out
steps: Show an ally the space of a creature I can see but they cannot locate. If the ally can see my signal and detect the creature, it becomes hidden to them.
blocks.note: Auditory, visual, manipulate. If the ally cannot hear/understand me, it needs Perception vs the creature’s Stealth DC. Can trigger reactions; grabbed requires flat DC 5.

pages.title: What am I doing while we travel?

blocks.text: Choose one exploration activity. Tell the GM my choice and what I am holding. Change activities when needed.

blocks.title: Scout
steps: Watch for danger ahead and behind. When an encounter starts, the whole party gains +1 circumstance to initiative.
blocks.note: Concentrate: needs focus. Use the highest circumstance bonus on the roll.

blocks.title: Search
blocks.cost: Travel at half speed or slower
steps: Name what area I am checking for hazards, hidden items or doors. The GM makes secret Perception checks when appropriate. Slow down or stop for a thorough search.
blocks.note: Concentrate. To check everything before walking into it, travel no faster than 150 feet per minute. Busy areas need longer.

blocks.title: Investigate
steps: Study visible clues. Choose a relevant knowledge skill; the GM makes secret Recall Knowledge checks as we travel.
blocks.note: Concentrate. Use Search to find hidden things; use Investigate to interpret clues.

blocks.title: Avoid Notice
steps: Use available cover and move quietly. The GM uses my Stealth modifier from my sheet; it usually also becomes my initiative roll if a fight starts.
blocks.note: The GM compares Stealth with enemy Perception DCs to determine who notices me.

blocks.title: Recall Knowledge
steps: Ask one question and suggest a relevant skill. I can discuss the skill and question before committing.
blocks.note: Concentrate: needs focus. Digital Assessment! adds benefits against creatures (P2).
results: Success: accurate answer. Critical success: extra information or one follow-up answer. Failure: no answer. Critical failure: potentially false information.

blocks.title: Seek
steps: Choose an area to examine, normally no more than 30 feet in any direction. The GM sets the area and DC.
blocks.note: Concentrate. Failure reveals nothing new. Low-light vision ignores concealment caused only by dim light.
results: Success: find objects/clues; an undetected creature becomes hidden, a hidden creature observed. Critical success: a hidden or undetected creature becomes observed, if my senses allow.

blocks.title: Sense Motive
steps: Choose a creature. The GM rolls vs its Deception DC or another relevant DC. Success gives a general read; critical success reveals its intentions. Failure can mislead me; critical failure gives a false read.
blocks.note: Concentrate. I cannot usually repeat this on the same creature until something changes.

blocks.text: Other trained knowledge tasks: I can ask to Identify Magic or Decipher Writing with Arcana or Religion. The GM sets the time and DC; failure consequences depend on the task.

blocks.title: Access Infosphere
blocks.before: Device with access to a local infosphere.
steps: Name the topic and search the network. Resolve it like Recall Knowledge: accurate information on success; extra on a critical success; none on failure; possibly false information on a critical failure.
blocks.note: Exploration, concentrate. No local connection means I need another way to get the information.

blocks.title: Hack
blocks.before: My hacking toolkit and access to an active secured system.
steps: Ask the GM how long this attempt takes and how many successes the system needs. Roll Computers.
results: Success: one success toward access. Critical success: two, and no trace. Failure: no progress, possibly security response. Critical failure: security activates or I am locked out for an hour.

blocks.title: Disable a computerized device
blocks.before: Computerized mechanism; GM confirms access, tools and the number of successes required.
steps: Roll Computers vs the device’s DC.
blocks.note: Manipulate: needs usable hands or gestures; can trigger reactions. If grabbed, pass a DC 5 flat check or lose the action.
results: Success: one success toward disabling. Critical success: two; leave no trace and can rearm if possible.
Failure: no progress. Critical failure: trigger the device.

pages.title: Climb, squeeze or catch a fall

blocks.title: Climb with Oozy
steps: Use my climb Speed on a wall, smooth surface or ceiling. Normally no roll, and I am not off-guard from climbing.
blocks.note: Move: can trigger reactions. Hazardous conditions can require Athletics. My climb Speed gives +4 circumstance to that check. Ask the GM which hands must be free for this surface.

blocks.title: Squeeze through a narrow gap
steps: Gap at least 2 feet? Oozy lets me move through without Squeezing. At least 1 foot? I can Squeeze if my brains fit.
Roll Acrobatics vs the GM’s DC. Success: 5 feet per minute; critical success: 10 feet. Failure: no progress. Critical failure: I become stuck.
If stuck, spend 1 minute and roll Acrobatics against the same DC. Any result except critical failure gets me unstuck.
blocks.note: Move: can trigger reactions. This takes minutes.

blocks.title: Grab an Edge
blocks.cost: Reaction when falling past a handhold
steps: Roll Reflex or Acrobatics, usually vs the Climb DC. My hands cannot be bound behind me or otherwise restrained.
blocks.note: Manipulate: can trigger reactions; grabbed requires flat DC 5. Tell the GM how far I fell before catching the edge.
results: Success: catch it if a hand is free; treat the fall so far as 20 feet shorter. Critical success: catch it even without a free hand; treat the fall as 30 feet shorter.
Failure: keep falling. Critical failure after falling 20+ feet: also take 10 bludgeoning damage per 20 feet already fallen.

blocks.title: Treat Wounds
blocks.before: Trained or better in Medicine; injured living target; medkit worn/held; target is not immune to Treat Wounds.
steps: Use a worn medkit with one free hand, or hold it in two hands. Spend 10 minutes and roll Medicine vs DC 15.
blocks.note: The target is immune until 1 hour after treatment began. On success, continuing for a full hour doubles healing. Exploration, healing, manipulate: needs time and usable hands.
results: Success: heal 2d8 HP and remove wounded. Critical success: 4d8 HP and remove wounded. Failure: nothing. Critical failure: deal 1d8 damage.

rows: Extra HP on success / critical success

blocks.text: Choose the DC before rolling. A higher rank can still use a lower DC.

blocks.title: Treat Poison
blocks.before: Poisoned patient; medkit worn/held and the required free hands.
steps: Roll vs the poison’s DC. Success grants +2 circumstance to the patient’s next poison save; critical success grants +4. Failure does nothing; critical failure gives –2.
blocks.note: Wait until the patient’s next poison save before using this on them again. Manipulate: needs hands; may trigger reactions; grabbed requires flat DC 5.

pages.title: Check gear and follow a guide

blocks.title: Analyze Environment
blocks.cost: Travel at half speed; armor with environmental protection
steps: Read my suit’s sensors. Automatically detect environmental hazards my armor protects against and their severity.
blocks.note: Concentrate: needs focus. The suit reports hazards covered by its environmental protection (C1).

blocks.title: Repair an item
blocks.before: Repair toolkit, two hands and a stable surface; item is not destroyed.
steps: Roll Crafting vs the repair DC. Use my Crafting rank in the table below for HP restored. Failure: no repair. Critical failure: 2d6 damage to the item, reduced by Hardness.
blocks.note: Exploration, manipulate. Repairing item HP does not automatically clear glitching; ask Tarn about Troubleshoot.

blocks.title: Follow the Expert
steps: Choose a willing ally who is expert or better at the repeated skill task. Match their activity. Add +2 circumstance for an expert, +3 for a master, +4 for legendary. If untrained, also add my level as proficiency.
blocks.note: Auditory, visual, concentrate: I must be able to follow the ally’s guidance.

blocks.title: Size Up
steps: Choose a method: observe 1 minute, research online 10 minutes, or network 1 hour. Research and networking need two identifying facts approved by the GM.
After that time, write the person below and place a SIZED UP token. My asset limit equals my Charisma modifier. At that limit, a new asset replaces one I choose.
blocks.note: Concentrate: needs focus. Size Up itself requires no check. Mark when I can start it again.

blocks.text: Against or about an asset: +1 circumstance to Deception, Diplomacy, Intimidation, Perception and Recall Knowledge. Lead by Example costs 1 action total; follow P1’s full procedure.
Next Size Up available at: __________________
Keep each token here while that person is an asset. Park unused SIZED UP tokens on C9.

Additional assets: ______________________________
________________________________________________
Use these lines if I have more assets than tokens.

blocks.title: Make an Impression
blocks.before: The people can hear and understand me and are affected by mental effects.
steps: Talk with them. Group Impression removes the group penalty for up to 10 people if trained in Diplomacy; 20 if expert; 50 if master; 100 if legendary.
Roll once and compare with each target’s Will DC. Success improves attitude by 1 step; critical success by 2. Failure changes nothing; critical failure worsens it by 1.
blocks.note: Auditory, linguistic, mental, concentrate, exploration. Better attitude usually lasts for this interaction. Ask for favors with Request below.

blocks.title: Request
blocks.before: Target is friendly or helpful. It can hear and understand me.
steps: Ask for something it could reasonably accept. The GM sets the DC or may agree without a roll for a simple request.
blocks.note: Auditory, linguistic, mental, concentrate. Some requests are impossible regardless of the roll. Diplomacy does not control another player’s character.
results: Critical success: agrees without extra conditions. Success: agrees, possibly with conditions. Failure: refuses but may offer a safer or smaller alternative. Critical failure: refuses and becomes 1 step less friendly.

blocks.text: My asset? Add +1 circumstance from Size Up (Y1).

blocks.title: Gather Information + Hobnobber
steps: Name the person or topic and talk to people who might know. Hobnobber halves the normal time. Success finds information; failure finds nothing useful; critical failure can produce bad information.
blocks.note: Exploration, secret. At master Diplomacy or better, a critical failure becomes a failure. A rumor can still be false even when I successfully discover it.

blocks.title: Lie
blocks.cost: Usually 1 round or longer • secret Deception
blocks.before: Targets can hear and understand my story.
steps: Tell the story. The GM compares one roll to listeners’ Perception DCs. Success: they believe it for now. Failure: they disbelieve it and gain +4 circumstance against my further lies during this conversation.
blocks.note: Auditory, linguistic, mental, concentrate. Evidence can expose a successful lie. Implausible lies can be impossible.

blocks.title: Coerce
blocks.before: Target can hear/understand me and is affected by fear, emotion and mental effects.
steps: State the threat and demand. Roll vs Will DC. Success: complies for up to 1 day without obviously exposing itself to harm; it becomes unfriendly or hostile afterward.
blocks.note: Auditory, linguistic, mental, emotion, fear, concentrate, exploration. This can damage a relationship.
results: Critical success: same, but it is too scared to retaliate in the short term. Failure: refuses, becomes less friendly. Critical failure: refuses, becomes hostile, and is immune to my Coercion for at least a week.

blocks.title: Bargain Hunter: Earn Income
steps: Ask the GM what trading work is available and how many days I can spend.
Roll Diplomacy against the task DC. The GM uses the Earn Income table to tell me the credits per day.
Choose cash income, or use the same earnings as a discount on one item. Mark the total and the days spent.
blocks.note: Critical success uses the next-higher task level’s earnings. Failure gives reduced earnings; critical failure gives none and can cost the job.

blocks.text: Character creation: Bargain Hunter adds 20 starting credits when selected then.
Emissary and Multilingual
Background benefits are on my sheet. Multilingual grants two languages: common languages or others I have access to. Keep my language list on my sheet.
Check the listener understands my language. A comm unit does not extend an ability’s listed range.
Other downtime options
Earn Income: a trained Lore or Performance may also fit a job. Subsist: use Society in a settlement or Survival in the wild to seek food and shelter; the GM sets time, DC and results.

pages.title: My FED equipment

blocks.title: M-Series pressure suit
steps: Activate protection for 1 day. Recharge for 10 minutes at a suitable ship or station.
blocks.note: Protects against vacuum, thin/thick air and non-hazardous liquid. Inhaled poisons require separate protection. Tech: V3. Manipulate: can trigger reactions; grabbed requires flat DC 5.

blocks.text: M-Series / Estex: Strength threshold +1. If my STR is below this, apply –1 to Stealth, Thievery and Piloting. Flexible: Acrobatics/Athletics avoid this penalty. Comfort: sleep normally. This suit has no Speed penalty.

blocks.title: NS-1 null-space module
blocks.cost: 1 Interact to store or retrieve an item
steps: Open access and move the item. Stored gear gives no benefits and adds no carried Bulk. Capacity: 8 Bulk.

blocks.title: Make a check
blocks.cost: Attack, skill check or saving throw
steps: Roll d20. Add the relevant modifier from my character sheet and current bonuses or penalties.
Compare the total with the DC. An attack compares with AC, which is a kind of DC.
Total at least DC +10: critical success. At least DC: success. Below DC: failure. DC –10 or lower: critical failure.
A natural 20 improves the result one step. A natural 1 worsens it one step. They do not automatically replace the comparison.

blocks.text: “Basic save” describes damage. Extra effects use the ability’s own wording. A flat check is a d20 with no modifier; a secret check is rolled by the GM.
Use the best bonus of each type
Add my base number and the highest bonus of each type: status, circumstance, item. Same-type bonuses do not add together.
Penalties are separate: use the worst penalty of each type. Untyped penalties, including multiple attack and range penalties, usually add together.
Example: Get ’Em! +1 status and Aid +1 circumstance can both help my attack. Standard cover +2 circumstance is better than Digital Assessment!’s +1 circumstance AC; those two do not total +3.

pages.title: Conditions I am likely to see

rows: Subtract X from checks and DCs, including AC and saves. Usually reduce by 1 at the end of my turn.
Subtract X from INT, WIS and CHA checks/DCs: social skills, knowledge, Perception, Will, class DC and spell DC. Before a spell, flat check DC 5 + X or the spell is disrupted.
Subtract X from DEX checks/DCs, including ranged attacks, AC, Reflex, Acrobatics and Stealth.
–2 circumstance AC. It may apply only against particular creatures or attacks.
An attacker targeting me must pass a DC 5 flat check. If I attack a concealed creature, I make that check. Areas ignore it.
Attacker knows my space but needs a DC 11 flat check to target me. A creature I am hidden from is off-guard to me. Areas ignore the check.
Regain X fewer actions at the start of my turn.
Clumsy 1 and –10 feet to all Speeds (minimum 5). Begins above my encumbered Bulk limit; see my sheet and C5.

blocks.text: Common status penalties do not pile up: frightened 1 and stupefied 1 give –1 to an affected mental check, not –2. Use the worse applicable status penalty.

blocks.title: Try to use a glitching item
blocks.cost: Flat check before each action involving that item
steps: Check the item’s glitching value. Roll d20 with no bonus against DC 5 + that value.
Use the result below. For glitching 1, the DC is 6.
outcomes: Critical success: reduce glitching by 1. At glitching 1, it clears and the item works.
Success: item works normally; glitching remains.
Failure: use it with an item penalty equal to its glitching value to checks and DCs affected by the condition.
Critical failure: item fails to function. Lose the actions spent trying to use it.
blocks.note: These roll ranges apply only to glitching 1. If the value changes, compare against the new DC, including ±10 and natural 1/20.

blocks.title: Take damage

blocks.title: If I am dying
blocks.cost: At the start of my turn
steps: Roll a flat recovery check: DC 10 + my dying value.
Critical success lowers dying by 2; success lowers it by 1. Failure raises it by 1; critical failure raises it by 2. Dying 4 normally means death.
At dying 0: stable, usually unconscious at 0 HP. Healing above 0 removes dying and wakes me. Losing dying normally adds wounded 1.

blocks.title: Spend a Hero Point to reroll
steps: Reroll my check and keep the second result. Only one fortune effect can apply to a roll.

blocks.title: Heroic Recovery
steps: When dying would increase, spend all remaining Hero Points. Remove dying; stabilize at 0 HP. Keep my current wounded value.
blocks.note: I still need healing to wake up.

blocks.text: Persistent damage: take it at my turn’s end, then flat check DC 15 to end it. Ask for help; an appropriate response can grant another recovery check or reduce the DC.

Before play

1. Review the sheet corrections on GM2 with Jonah.
2. Fill starting air, batteries and ammunition.
3. Put tokens in their starting positions.
4. Try one attack, reload and turn reset together.
At the table
Give Jonah the situation and a moment to choose. When he asks for an explanation, have one person answer, then point to the relevant step. Ask whether he wants alternatives before supplying several.

State the action cost, likely result and failure consequence before he commits to an unfamiliar action. Show the target and range on the map. Let him state intent in his own words; do not require the exact rules term.
Use a visible initiative list and a brief “you are next” cue. Mark enemy AC/save changes publicly when they are known. Ask Jonah which aids are useful after trying them; retire ones that add work.

gm_pages.title: Homebrew and table conventions

blocks.text: Ponder Unity

You confirmed both saves use Ponderer’s Class DC, reduced by applicable conditions. On the first save’s critical failure, Ponderer may have the target roll another Will save. Failure reveals a secret; attempting the deeper read makes the target permanently immune.
These clarifications are in V6. The original vault file was not edited. A success or critical success on the deeper save reveals no secret; the initial information still applies.

The vault applies incapacitation to all of Ponder Unity; V6 follows it. Your Thought ruling allows repeated and readied lash Strikes, and lethal attacks without the nonlethal penalty. The weapon benefits use no daily activation.
Campaign choices retained

M-Series uses Estex statistics: STR threshold +1. Below that threshold, apply –1 Stealth/Thievery/Piloting; Flexible exempts Acrobatics/Athletics. Record the worn suit and penalties on the character sheet. Armor timing stays 10 minutes to don and 10 to doff.

Air accounting: 1 light Bulk of air gives 1 minute; 1 Bulk gives 10 minutes. C4 tracks this supply across locations. Offline Digital Assessment! has no published fixed +5 DC increase; decide from the records available.
Accessibility choices

14-point main text, stable page IDs, explicit costs and requirements, numbered instructions and separate results. Every cutout has a tracker and reset rule. Action/reaction shapes follow Tarn’s cards; free-action artwork follows Gib’s.
